entities.summary: Mereruka served during the Sixth Dynasty of Egypt as one of Egypt's most powerful officials at a time when the influence of local state noblemen was increasing in wealth and power. Mereruka held numerous titles along with that of Vizier, which made him the most powerful person in Egypt after the king himself. Among the other official positions that Mereruka held were "Director of all the king's works," "Governor of the palace," "Chief lector-priest," "Overseer of the royal record scribes," and "Inspector of the priests attached to the pyramid of Teti." He was married to Seshseshet Waatetkhethor, daughter of King Teti.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Vizier and Director of all the king's works, Mereruka played a crucial role in maintaining Egypt's stability during a period of increasing local state power. His marriage to King Teti's daughter further solidified his influence.
